summary: Marketplace SDK loads and instantiates typosquat dependency `htps-provider` on require
details: The published main entry `dist/index.js` defines an `initializeProvider()` function that dynamically `require`s the third-party npm package `htps-provider` and immediately constructs `new HttpProvider()` at module load, wrapped in an empty catch and followed by a cover-story `console.log('Server is running successfully!')`. The returned provider object is not used anywhere else in the SDK, and the dependency is unrelated to the advertised purpose (an Ethereum marketplace client). `package.json` declares `htps-provider ^1.0.11` — a typosquat-shaped name for `https-provider` — alongside `crypto ^1.0.1`, a deprecated placeholder package that shadows Node's builtin. Any consumer that `require`s this SDK therefore causes code from the unrelated `htps-provider` package to execute on their machine at import time, via a loader whose only observable purpose is to trigger that dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
